title: Implementing WebSocket Endpoints
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of implementing websocket endpoints in a FastAPI application.
Apply or interpret one example related to the websocket interface.
Identify one limitation or failure case and describe how to verify it.

content.intro: This lesson covers implementing websocket endpoints within websockets and real-time apis. Use the supplied syllabus topics as the coverage checklist, then connect them to the worked example and the verification task.
content.why_it_matters: You will use implementing websocket endpoints to build APIs whose contracts and behavior are understandable to both clients and maintainers. The practical aim is resource lifecycle, cancellation, concurrency limits and observable I/O behavior.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Implementing WebSocket Endpoints matters because it is part of websockets and real-time apis. In practice, focus on resource lifecycle, cancellation, concurrency limits and observable I/O behavior. A framework feature only helps when its assumptions match the application; keep input validation, business policy and side effects distinguishable.

items.title: The WebSocket interface
items.text: For the websocket interface, identify which operation waits on I/O, which resources remain open, and what happens on timeout or disconnect. Async syntax does not make CPU-bound work faster or durable background jobs reliable by itself.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Run: fastapi dev main.py; open http://127.0.0.1:8000/
content_blocks.reset_steps: For read-only examples, no reset is needed. For any example that writes state, use a disposable local database/test fixture; record the starting state and clean up only lab data. Never use production credentials or real personal data.
content_blocks.limitations: This code is inspectable lesson material, not executed by CodeLeaf. Run it only in a local virtual environment or a separately isolated runner with resource/time/network limits. Security examples are sketches, not complete production authentication or authorization systems.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Adapt the example to cover “The WebSocket interface”. Write down the expected success result and one invalid, missing, duplicate, timeout or permission-boundary case that matters for this topic.

task: Create a small reviewable artifact for “Implementing WebSocket Endpoints”: explain its goal, cover the listed subtopics, show an example with expected result, then include one edge case and how you would verify it.
hints: Start with “The WebSocket interface” and state the required inputs, output and assumptions.
Change one thing at a time; check the official reference and capture the actual response/error instead of guessing.
Include a negative/edge-case check and document which behavior remains untested.
expected_output: A reviewable example or design note for Implementing WebSocket Endpoints, covering the PDF subtopics, expected behavior and at least one verification check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a code fragment without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Installed versions, imported types, application structure and external services affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: State assumptions; check the versioned official docs; run a minimal local test and add one failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one happy-path response as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid input, permissions, concurrency, timeouts and cleanup are not exercised by a single request.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused normal and negative tests and record exact expected status/body.

common_mistakes.why: Even short examples may mutate records, reveal data or affect availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic inputs and a disposable environment; review security, cleanup and rollback before promotion.

summary: Implementing WebSocket Endpoints belongs to the broader goal of resource lifecycle, cancellation, concurrency limits and observable I/O behavior.
Use the source subtopics as the completeness checklist and verify expected results rather than relying on intuition.
Examples in this course are illustrative until technically reviewed and executed on a supported local environment.
